solution:
In similar triangles the corresponding angles are congruent and the corresponding sides are in proportion. The similarity \(\triangle XYZ \sim \triangle LMN\) fixes the correspondence X - L, Y - M, Z - N.
The corresponding angles are \(\angle X \cong \angle L\), \(\angle Y \cong \angle M\) and \(\angle Z \cong \angle N\).
The ratios of the corresponding sides are \(\frac{XY}{LM} = \frac{YZ}{MN} = \frac{XZ}{LN}\).

Since \(\triangle XYZ \sim \triangle PQR\), the corresponding sides are in proportion, so \(\frac{XY}{PQ} = \frac{YZ}{QR} = \frac{XZ}{PR}\).
Here \(\frac{XY}{PQ} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\), so each side of \(\triangle PQR\) is twice the corresponding side of \(\triangle XYZ\).
From \(\frac{YZ}{QR} = \frac{1}{2}\), \(QR = 2 \times YZ = 2 \times 6 = 12\) cm.
From \(\frac{XZ}{PR} = \frac{1}{2}\), \(PR = 2 \times XZ = 2 \times 5 = 10\) cm.
Hence QR = 12 cm and PR = 10 cm.

diagramNote: A pair of similar triangles side by side, the smaller labelled ABC with AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CA = 5 cm and the larger labelled PQR with PQ = 6 cm, QR = 8 cm, RP = 10 cm; one arc at A and P, two arcs at B and Q, three arcs at C and R.
solution:
Draw any triangle and label it \(\triangle ABC\). Beside it draw a second triangle \(\triangle PQR\) of the same shape but a different size, and label it so that the correspondence is A - P, B - Q, C - R.
Show the corresponding angles by the same signs: one arc at \(\angle A\) and at \(\angle P\), two arcs at \(\angle B\) and at \(\angle Q\), three arcs at \(\angle C\) and at \(\angle R\). These marks record that \(\angle A \cong \angle P\), \(\angle B \cong \angle Q\) and \(\angle C \cong \angle R\).
Now write lengths on the sides that are in proportion. For example, mark AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CA = 5 cm on the first triangle and PQ = 6 cm, QR = 8 cm, RP = 10 cm on the second. Then \(\frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{3}{6}\), \(\frac{BC}{QR} = \frac{4}{8}\) and \(\frac{CA}{RP} = \frac{5}{10}\), each of which equals \(\frac{1}{2}\), so the corresponding sides are in proportion and the second triangle is the first one drawn at twice the size.
Hence the sketch shows \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR\), with equal angles marked by the same signs and corresponding sides in the ratio \(1 : 2\).
